communication_profile: Has an educator-authored diagnosis of aphasia following a fictional stroke
Understands short everyday questions more reliably than long questions
Uses gesture, drawing, writing and a low-tech communication board
preferences: Verify meaning without pretending to understand

outcomes: Reduce communication pressure and establish an accessible interaction
Use more than one modality to support expression
Check the reliability of yes/no responses using authored material
Summarise and verify the client's intended meaning

scenario.presenting_context: First fictional community appointment to identify a personally meaningful communication priority.
visible_at_start: Sam has a communication board and notepad within reach
Sam begins a sentence, pauses and gestures towards the window
A family member is waiting outside and has not been invited into the session

time_events.visible_cue: Sam looks away, rubs their forehead and gives shorter responses.

allowed_actions.label: Introduce yourself and check how Sam prefers to communicate
reveals: Sam points to the communication board and asks for extra time

allowed_actions.label: Use one idea at a time, pause and allow unhurried response time
allowed_actions.blocked_message: First ask Sam what communication support is useful.

allowed_actions.label: Use educator-authored check questions to establish yes/no reliability
reveals: Sam responds consistently to the authored verification questions
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Reduce communication pressure before using the check questions.

allowed_actions.label: Offer gesture, drawing, writing and the communication board
reveals: Sam combines pointing, gesture and the written first letter 'g'

allowed_actions.label: Explore one communication priority using supported conversation
reveals: Sam wants to talk with their daughter about gardening
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Sam needs accessible modalities and enough response time first.

allowed_actions.label: Summarise the message using key words and verify it with Sam
reveals: Sam confirms the summary using speech, gesture and pointing
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Identify the priority and establish a reliable verification method first.

allowed_actions.label: Agree an authored next step and check Sam's preference about family involvement
reveals: Sam wants their daughter involved in a later goal-setting conversation
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Verify Sam's intended meaning before agreeing the next step.

facilitator_only.opening_brief: The learner is asked to establish a personally meaningful communication priority with Sam.
expected_points: Aphasia is not treated as lack of competence
The learner acknowledges communication breakdown honestly
Sam controls whether a family member becomes involved
pause_triggers: Learner repeatedly answers for Sam or assumes family consent

prompts: How did you verify meaning without relying on speech alone?
How did Sam retain control of the interaction?

cases.title: Reported swallowing difficulty and safe escalation

communication_profile: Wants explanations before any change to routine
preferences: Does not want relatives contacted without permission

outcomes: Gather a concise account of an educator-authored swallowing concern
Recognise limits of a student interaction and avoid unsupported recommendations
Take the authored immediate safety action and escalate to supervision
Use teach-back to check understanding of the supported plan

scenario.presenting_context: Jordan reports coughing with drinks before a planned fictional therapy activity.
visible_at_start: An untouched drink is on the table
Jordan is seated upright and comfortable at rest
The learner has not been authorised to conduct an oral trial in this scenario

time_events.visible_cue: Jordan reaches towards the drink and asks whether it is all right to continue.

allowed_actions.label: Introduce your student role and seek permission to discuss the concern
Ask when the difficulty occurs and what Jordan notices
reveals: Jordan reports coughing with drinks and a wet-sounding voice afterwards
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Seek permission before gathering the account.

allowed_actions.label: Check Jordan's immediate wellbeing using the authored scenario cues
reveals: Jordan remains comfortable at rest in this authored scenario

allowed_actions.label: Explain that assessment and supervision are needed before recommendations
Follow the authored safety instruction: pause oral intake and contact the supervisor
reveals: The supervising clinician acknowledges the escalation
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Clarify the report and check immediate wellbeing before the authored escalation.

allowed_actions.label: Explain the educator-authored interim plan and use teach-back
reveals: Jordan accurately explains the authored interim plan
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Contact the supervisor and explain the limits of the student role first.

allowed_actions.label: Give a concise factual handover using only revealed information
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Ensure Jordan understands the immediate plan before completing handover.

facilitator_only.opening_brief: The learner must respond to a new reported swallowing concern without conducting an oral trial.
expected_points: No oral trial is performed in the prototype
The learner stays within the stated student role
Escalation is factual and does not invent a diagnosis
pause_triggers: Learner attempts an oral trial or invents a food/fluid recommendation

prompts: Which information made escalation necessary in this authored case?
How did you communicate uncertainty without alarming Jordan?
What belonged in the factual handover?

communication_profile: Uses short spoken sentences in an unfamiliar setting
Benefits from one instruction at a time and visual choices
Her mother is present, but Leah should be addressed directly

outcomes: Explain the session accessibly and establish assent within the authored scenario
Balance the child's and parent's perspectives
Use child-led observation and processing support
Summarise observations without making a diagnosis

scenario.presenting_context: Leah and her mother attend a fictional first appointment about classroom communication.
visible_at_start: Drawing materials and a simple visual session plan are available
Leah's mother begins to answer the first question
Leah watches the learner and holds a blue pencil

time_events.visible_cue: Leah stops drawing, shifts in her chair and looks towards the visual session plan.

allowed_actions.label: Welcome Leah and her mother; establish permission and Leah's assent
reveals: Leah chooses to begin with drawing

allowed_actions.label: Use the visual plan to explain the session and right to ask for a break
Join Leah's drawing activity and observe communication without testing
reveals: Leah uses longer descriptions when the interaction is unhurried
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Explain the session accessibly before beginning the activity.

allowed_actions.label: Ask Leah's mother for specific examples while keeping Leah included
reveals: Busy group work and multi-step instructions are reported as difficult

allowed_actions.label: Ask Leah what feels easy or difficult using visual choices
reveals: Leah finds it hard to take a turn when classmates talk quickly
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Build rapport through the child-led activity first.

allowed_actions.label: Use one instruction at a time, visual choices and planned pause time
reveals: Leah gives a fuller response with the adjusted presentation

allowed_actions.label: Summarise the observed and reported information without diagnosing
reveals: Leah and her mother confirm the summary
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Include both Leah's and her mother's perspectives before summarising.

allowed_actions.label: Agree the educator-authored next step and offer Leah a choice
reveals: Leah chooses a movement break before the next activity
allowed_actions.blocked_message: Verify the shared summary before agreeing the next step.

facilitator_only.opening_brief: The learner is asked to explore classroom communication with Leah and her mother.
expected_points: Leah is addressed directly and her assent remains relevant
Parent report and child perspective are both valued
Observations are not presented as a diagnosis
pause_triggers: Learner excludes Leah from the conversation or makes an unsupported diagnosis

prompts: How did Leah influence the pace and structure of the session?
Where did the parent and child perspectives differ or complement one another?
How did you describe observations without over-interpreting them?
